## Edges that say how papers relate

The graph stores **quadruples**: `<paper1, citation position, citation semantics, paper2>`. Position and semantics together play the role of the relation in an ordinary knowledge-graph triple.

- **Citation position** is where the reference appears in the citing paper's text, used as a measure of how important the citation is. (The paper does not spell out how positions map to importance.)
- **Citation semantics** is one of five categories:
  - **B&E** Based on and Extension
  - **S&S** Support and Supplement
  - **C&A** Contrast and Alternative
  - **Q&A** Question and Refutation
  - **M/I** Simple Mention or Irrelevant

To fill these in, the **SciPDF Parser** splits papers into paragraphs, and an LLM is prompted to pull out the cited references and decide which of the five labels best describes each citation.

This is what lets the system distinguish a paper that builds on a predecessor from one that merely name-drops it. The paper does not report how accurate this LLM labelling is.
